analysis.title: Investor Positioning and Flows - The Spring Is Coiled Again: Upgrading Tech Back To Overweight
key_insights: DB upgrades Tech (mega-cap growth and Tech, MCG & Tech) tactically back to overweight from neutral, three weeks after the Oct 9 downgrade. The stated reason is that performance, positioning and growth perception have reset and risk-reward now favors Tech.

MCG & Tech has underperformed the rest of the S&P 500 by over 16pp in the last three weeks. It fell 11% while the rest of the S&P 500 rose almost 6%, taking relative performance to the bottom of its decade-long trend channel.
From the bottom of the channel, MCG & Tech relative performance has turned up 5 times in the last 2.5 years. DB notes it can fall further, as it did around Liberation Day and the Iran War.
On average, past rotations into Tech saw Tech rise 32% and outperform the rest of the S&P 500 by 30pp. The S&P 500 rose 16% over 3 months on average in those rotations.

Tech positioning has fallen from clearly elevated levels three weeks ago to neutral (40th percentile). DB says this is in line with earnings growth of around 10%, against about 47% in Q3 and 36% expected by consensus by the end of next year.
DB reads Tech positioning as already pricing significant risk around AI demand and potential regulation and scrutiny after the US mid-term elections next week.

Large-cap equity positioning is modestly overweight (66th percentile). Discretionary investors are neutral (48th percentile in the text, 21% in Figure 13), in line with mid-single-digit earnings growth, well below S&P 500 earnings growth.

Q3 earnings growth is on track for 31% y/y. Tech and Energy account for about 3/4 of it, but growth excluding Tech and Energy is 12% and the median S&P 500 company is growing 14.4%, both near 2-decade highs outside recession rebounds.
Positioning in sectors outside Tech is very low (6th percentile) and small-cap positioning is low (22nd percentile), leaving room to catch up with earnings growth.
On post-midterm policy risk, DB says a lot is priced in. Before the 2024 election, large-cap positioning was similar to now but in line with earnings growth, whereas now it is well below.
Oil (WTI $102.0) is 65% above DB's medium-term fair value of $61.8, based on global growth and the US dollar. The premium is close to the peak in the first month of the Iran war.
Near-month Brent futures are more than 15% above the 6th-month contract, similar to prior large oil-supply disruptions, so the oil market is pricing significant supply disruption.
Systematic positioning is high: 79th percentile overall, vol-control equity allocation 77th, risk-parity equity weight 84th, CTA overall equity 58th (SPX 82nd, NDX 55th, RTY 29th).
CTAs are short-ish bonds (10th percentile overall) and heavily short GBP (0th percentile), CAD (6th), NZD (3rd), EUR (8th) and CHF (9th), while long oil at the 79th percentile.
AAII sentiment: bearish share is at the 84th percentile since 1987 and the bull-minus-bear spread is at the 29th percentile. Net call volume is at the 86th percentile.
Equity L/S hedge fund beta to the S&P 500 is at the 89th percentile on both 1m and 3m rolling windows. Mutual fund 3m beta is at the 23rd percentile.
DB S&P 500 forecasts: 2026 target 8000, 2026 EPS $358, 2027 EPS $420.

sector_views.rationale: Tactical upgrade from neutral. Relative performance is at the bottom of its trend channel and positioning has reset to neutral while earnings growth remains strong.
Positioning is very low (6th percentile) against 12% growth ex-Tech and Energy, so there is room to catch up. DB gives no explicit rating.
Positioning is low (22nd percentile). DB gives no explicit rating.
Energy positioning is at the 80th percentile and Energy contributes to Q3 earnings growth. DB gives no explicit rating.

earnings_insights: S&P 500 Q3 2026 blended EPS growth is on track for 31% y/y (blended, assumes companies yet to report beat at the current beat rate). Tech and Energy account for about 3/4 of it.
S&P 500 Q3 2026 EPS growth excluding Tech and Energy is 12% y/y and the median company is growing 14.4% y/y (blended), both around 2-decade highs outside recession rebounds.
Tech earnings growth was around 47% in Q3 and consensus expects 36% by the end of next year. DB says current Tech positioning is consistent with growth of only about 10%.
DB S&P 500 EPS forecasts: $358 for 2026 and $420 for 2027.

Backwardation similar to past large oil-supply disruptions, so the market is already pricing significant supply disruption.

trade_ideas.description: Tactical overweight in Tech (mega-cap growth and Tech) versus neutral, reversing the Oct 9 downgrade
trade_ideas.rationale: Relative performance is at the bottom of its decade-long trend channel and positioning has fallen to neutral, in line with about 10% earnings growth against much higher actual growth.
trade_ideas.risk: Tech can fall further around large exogenous shocks, as it did around Liberation Day and the Iran War. Post-midterm regulation and renewed geopolitical escalation are also named.

risk_factors: Regulation targeting Tech after the US mid-term elections next week.
Renewed geopolitical escalation and oil-supply disruption.
Relative performance of Tech can fall below the bottom of its trend channel around large exogenous shocks.
AI-demand concerns and a sharp deceleration in earnings growth from about 47% in Q3.
charts_described: Figure 1: MCG & Tech ratio to the rest of the S&P 500 has gone from the top to the bottom of its long-run trend channel in three weeks (trend growth 14.2% annualized, band +/-10%).
Figure 2: five rotations into Tech and five away in the last 2.5 years. The latest rotation away (Oct 7 to Oct 30, 18 trading days) saw MCG & Tech -10.7% and the S&P 500 -2.8%.
Oil price fair value chart: WTI current $102.0, fair value $61.8, 65.0% deviation (regression sample Feb 2000 to Dec 2013, R-squared 84%).
Brent 1st-month to 6th-month futures ratio is elevated, similar to prior supply disruptions.
vol_and_positioning: Consolidated equity positioning is at the 44th percentile since 2010. Discretionary is at the 21st percentile and systematic at the 79th (Figure 13).
Systematic strategies: vol-control equity allocation 77th percentile, CTA equity 58th, risk-parity equity weight 84th percentile (US 88th, DM ex-US 83rd, EM 75th).

MCG & Tech positioning is at the 40th percentile. Financials 23rd, Energy 80th, Consumer cyclicals 17th, Industrial cyclicals 35th, Materials 16th, Consumer Staples 15th, Healthcare 52nd, Real Estate 28th, Utilities 2nd, small caps 22nd.
AAII bullish is at the 52nd percentile, bearish at the 84th, neutral at the 10th, and the bull-minus-bear spread at the 29th.
Equity call/put volume ratio is at the 57th percentile and total net call volume at the 86th percentile (data as of Oct 29).
CTA percentiles: SPX 82%, NDX 55%, RTY 29%, Europe 57%, Japan 56%, EM 39%. Bonds overall 10%, US 21%, Europe 16%, UK 18%, Japan 27%.
CTA FX percentiles: AUD 68%, EUR 8%, JPY 21%, CAD 6%, CHF 9%, GBP 0%, NZD 3%. Oil 79%.
Equity L/S hedge fund beta is at the 89th percentile (1m and 3m). Large-cap mutual fund beta is at the 59th (1m) and 23rd (3m) percentile.
Bond futures positioning as % of open interest (Oct 20): SOFR -18.6%, 2y -18.9%, 5y -16.0%, 10y -13.0%, 30y -3.8%, Ultra T-bond -15.9%.
Currency futures positioning as % of open interest (Oct 20): NZD -44%, AUD -38%, GBP -32%, CAD -19%, Euro -15%, CHF -13%, MXN 6%, USD trade-weighted 15%, JPY 18%, BRL 24%.
S&P 500 weekly announced buybacks 3-month sum is $192bn, with $220bn for announced buybacks by sector over the last 3 months.
geopolitical: Renewed geopolitical escalation risk, with DB saying oil is already pricing significant supply disruptions.
The Iran war, referenced as a prior shock and the peak of the oil premium in its first month.
Potential regulation targeting Tech after the US mid-term elections next week.

tension_points.bull_case: Tech relative performance is at the bottom of its trend channel, positioning has reset to neutral against strong earnings growth, and past rotations into Tech averaged a 32% gain.
tension_points.bear_case: Regulation targeting Tech after the US mid-terms, AI-demand concerns and geopolitical escalation could push Tech lower, as it fell further around Liberation Day and the Iran War.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A large exogenous shock such as those around Liberation Day or the Iran War, which pushed relative performance below the channel bottom.
